transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I hardly eat right anymore. Some days it's just... coffee and maybe a piece of bread for the whole day. I just don't have an appetite for anything. And my pants are hanging loose on me now, so I know I've lost a good bit of weight. I just figured I needed to come in and see someone about it.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days, I just... I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like I already know nothing good is waiting for me that day, so I don't even want to try. I don't really care about doing much of anything anymore. I just want to... I don't know, just keep my head down.
Have you been feeling guilty or like you're not worth much lately? Or maybe feeling like you're a failure or have let people down?

Yeah, I do. I just... I keep thinking I'm no good. Since I lost that job, my relatives have been having to help me out with things, and it just eats at me. I sit there and I replay every mistake I've made... just over and over in my head. It really feels like I just ruined everything.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live anymore, or thinking about death?

No, not really. I mean, I feel awful and useless, like I said, but... I haven't been thinking about dying or anything like that. I don't want to hurt myself. I just... I just want to feel better, I guess. Or at least not feel like this all the time. But no thoughts about ending it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been... I'd say about five months now. This whole depressed spell has just been hanging over me for that long.
Have you noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, that you're more restless or fidgety than before?

Yeah... I guess I have. Or, well, mostly my family notices it. They tell me I move like I'm walking through mud these days. And with talking... sometimes it just takes me a really long time to answer even a simple question. I don't feel restless or anything like that, just... really slow.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident, even if it was for a short time?

Yeah, actually. Right after I got fired from my last job, I had a spell like that. You'd think I'd be upset, but I just felt... I don't know, really fired up. Like I was kind of untouchable. But I was also pretty edgy. I would snap at people fast if they told me I should slow down.
How long did that unusually high and energetic feeling last when you felt untouchable after losing your job?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's... it's hard to remember exactly how long it was. I wasn't really keeping track of time back then. It just sort of happened, but I couldn't give you an exact number of days or anything like that.
Can you estimate how many days or weeks that high and energetic feeling lasted after you lost your job?

I really can't give you a good guess. I don't want to just make something up. It could have been a few days, or... maybe a couple of weeks? It's just all a blur now. My head really wasn't in a place to count the days, so I honestly just don't know.
Can you think back to that time after you lost your job when you felt unusually high and energetic—did that feeling last for at least four full days in a row without stopping?

I really just can't say for sure. Like I was telling you, I wasn't keeping track of the time. I mean... maybe? It could have been four days straight, but I can't promise you that. I just remember being in that headspace, not what day of the week it was. I'm sorry, I just don't have a solid answer for you on that.
During that time when you felt unusually high and energetic after losing your job, did you need less sleep than usual, like only sleeping a few hours a night and still feeling rested?

Yeah, that part I actually remember. Back then, I was sleeping... maybe two or three hours a night. But I wasn't tired at all. I'd just jump right up like I had a full night's rest. I just didn't really feel like I needed it, I guess.

During that time when you felt unusually high and energetic after losing your job, did you find yourself doing a lot more things — like starting new projects, making big plans, or being much more active than usual?

Yeah, I did. I was... well, I started calling up old tenants, making all these lists. I was pricing out tools and trying to line up handyman work all day long. It was just way more than I ever did before.
